title: Google's new Gemini tiers cut free users to its weakest model and lock $5/month subscribers out of Pro
key_facts: Starting in October 2026, Google restricts Gemini model access for personal accounts without a subscription to the smallest model, Flash-Lite.
The current free tier offers 3.6 Flash and some access to 3.1 Pro; both are removed from the free tier.
AI Plus subscribers ($4.99 a month) lose Pro access and keep only Flash-Lite and Flash.
All three models (Flash-Lite, Flash, Pro) require AI Pro ($19.99 a month) or AI Ultra ($99.99 or $199.99 a month).
The Decoder says the setup mirrors OpenAI's freemium model for ChatGPT and that the tier details are on Google's support page.
The Decoder judges the real-world impact likely small, since most casual users do not know which model they use and power users mostly already pay.
The Decoder suggests Google may be preparing for the larger, costlier Gemini 4 Argon.
quote_evidence: Without a subscription, users will only get the smallest model, "Flash-Lite."
AI Plus subscribers ($4.99/month) lose access to Pro and can only use Flash-Lite and Flash.
The real-world impact is likely small.
why_it_matters_hint: Free and $5 Gemini users are pushed to weaker models, in line with OpenAI's paid-tier approach.
event_date: October 2026 (effective date of the new tiers)
notes: Single outlet; The Decoder cites Google's support page for tier details but the article was short (about 1,100 characters). The impact assessment and the Gemini 4 Argon link are The Decoder's own analysis, not Google statements.
